Figure 1: Matrix-mixer view of RoPE and RoVE. RoPE factorises into (a) position-sensitive attention weights and (b) a constant shared value projection WV across all offsets (c). (d) RoVE replaces WV with the offset-indexed family ψδ = RδWV , (e) producing a block-Toeplitz mixer whose diagonals rotate systematically with relative offset, the signature of an attentive convolution.

Figure 2: Visualization of the circuits of the one-layer attention-only transformer for RoPE (left; adapted from Elhage et al. (2021)) and RoVE (right). In standard RoPE, we have as many bifurcations from the residual stream as there are attention heads hi at that layer. In RoVE we obtain new bifurcations associated with each displacement δ.
